name: API Rate-Window Clock
description: Enter cache-hit, fresh-input, and output tokens to see a DeepSeek batch's declared cost now versus the next cheaper UTC price window.
data_source: DeepSeek English and Chinese Models & Pricing pages
records: 2 current model IDs, 2 language authority surfaces, 2 weekday peak windows with a Chinese-public-holiday exclusion, 1 superseded table kept as history
detail: Static client-side calculator for DeepSeek's declared weekday peak/off-peak API schedule. Select a current model, enter cache-hit input, cache-miss input, and output tokens, and choose now or a planned local time. The result shows the selected USD band, component rates, cost, effective basis, and earliest cheaper boundary with wait time and savings. Chinese public holidays are off-peak all day, but no holiday list is published, so the user declares the start's Beijing date and every weekday-peak result shows the holiday price. English and Chinese pricing pages are parsed independently and semantic-hash pinned; source conflict or missing rates disable calculation rather than producing a zero or average.
asymmetry: API customers can see the vendor's individual prices yet still cannot answer the launch-time question without translating weekdays, UTC windows, effective dates, and separate cache/input/output rates. Vendors collect the higher charge when otherwise identical workloads drift into peak periods; independent developers and small teams benefit from a decision-ready timing estimate before starting a long batch.
pipeline_note: Dependency-free EN/ZH table parser, normalized semantic pin, effective-dated declarative rate schema, weekday-aware Python/JavaScript mirrors, shared fixture table, full-object differential parity, and browser boundary smoke. Current raw HTML and SHA-256 receipts are archived.
